prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map captures the 3D geometry of a small room corner containing a recessed multi-shelf altar on the left wall and a barred window on the right wall, with three men standing at distinct depth tiers. A man in the left foreground holding a small booklet and a man cropped on the right foreground edge are both very bright and within arm's reach of the camera wearer at roughly 0.6 to 1.0 metres (separated from each other by about 1.0 to 1.2 metres), while a third man stands further back in the centre-right at roughly 1.8 to 2.2 metres, about 1.2 metres beyond the foreground pair. Across the 5 frames, the left foreground man faces away and slightly right toward the altar while shifting slightly closer to the camera, the right foreground man faces left with his head and body mostly cropped out of view in frames 2, 4, and 5 leaving only his hands visible at the bottom-right, and the background man faces left toward the altar with the tray of red petals in his left hand and shelf items within his arm's reach; none of the three look toward the camera wearer. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the side walls, the recessed steps of the altar shelves, and the clear depth separation between the foreground men's shoulders and the background man immediately apparent. However, the map is unreliable inside the dark recess of the altar where lit flames and shiny brass vessels flatten into uniform dark patches, and around thin structures like the window bars and the right foreground man's fingers which blur into adjacent background depths.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates the foreground and midground figures as distinct 2D silhouettes against a black background, separating the left foreground man (~0.7 to 0.9 metres away, cropped below the upper back), the centre-right standing man (~2.0 metres away, cropped below the knees), and the right-edge man (~0.8 metres away, severely occluded by the right frame boundary). Across the 5 frames, the masks show the left man remaining in front-left facing away-right while partially occluding the lower altar shelf, the background man standing in front-centre facing left with his extended right arm reaching toward the shelf in frames 1 to 3 before retracting to his tray in frames 4 to 5, and the right-side man appearing as a torso and head in frames 1 and 3, completely disappearing in frames 2 and 5, and reducing to a lower-corner mask in frame 4. While the map provides crisp boundary contours between overlapping people and flags small held or wall-hung items within arm's reach of the participants—such as the small booklet in the left man's hands (frame 1), the red bag hanging on the far-left wall edge (frame 2), and the tray held at waist height by the background man (frame 1)—it lacks direct distance values without RGB context. Furthermore, the map is highly unreliable in both class labels and temporal consistency: it misclassifies the booklet as a 'cell phone', the flower tray as a 'pizza', the wall-hung bag as a 'handbag', and the right-hand barred window wall as a 'refrigerator' (frames 1 and 4) or 'oven' (frame 3), while completely dropping all object and background masks in several frames and missing the right-edge man's hands in frames 2 and 5.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map renders sparse 2D joint and bone keypoints on a black background, capturing the torso, arm, and facial-profile orientation of the standing man ~2.0 metres away in the centre-right and isolated keypoints for the closer men (~0.6 to 1.0 metres away) when detected. In frames 3 and 5, the yellow upper-body skeleton of the background man shows his shoulders, elbows, and wrists angled to the left with head keypoints facing left and downward toward the tray held within his arm's reach, confirming he never looks toward the camera wearer, while magenta hand meshes in frame 2 (centre) and frame 5 (bottom-right) resolve the fine finger articulations of the background man's right hand and the right-foreground man's clasped hands. Compared to the RGB image, the skeleton overlays explicitly trace joint angles, torso tilt, and overlapping finger positions free of lighting clutter or skin-tone blending. However, this map is extremely sparse and unreliable across the sequence: it completely misses all three people in frame 4, misses the background man's body in frames 1 and 2, fails to track the left foreground man except for a fragmented head-and-shoulder cluster in frame 1 because his back is turned and cropped, and omits the entire room layout, altar shelves, and held objects.
